keyFindings.description:
New panic on untrusted markdown. splitAtEvenEscapedPipes adds a split-off cell with row.InsertAfter(row, cell, next). When cell is the row's last child, goldmark's InsertAfter calls InsertBefore(self, nil, ...), which adds 1 to childCount and then AppendChild adds 1 again (goldmark ast.go:376-384, 353-366), so row.ChildCount() exceeds the real cell count. keepEscapedClosingPipes' guard `written > row.ChildCount()` (table.go:652) then lets its loop walk past the last cell and dereference nil. Reproduced at aef61f9e with a throwaway test: Parse("| h | i |
| --- | --- |
| a | b \\| \|
") returns ErrPanic (logged at ERROR with a stack); the same row without the escaped closing pipe gets the ErrSchema wide-row refusal; the base b6d8fa2a parses it with no error. The deep review saw 27 panics in 4,000 random rows at the head, 0 at the base. Census item 2 says such rows are refused. Fix: AppendChild when cell.NextSibling() == nil, InsertBefore(row, cell.NextSibling(), next) otherwise (or count cells by walking siblings), and add the row as a regression case expecting the wide-row ErrSchema.

The doc-edit help says code whose text has a backslash right before a | is INVALID_OP; only an odd run is refused, and code `a\\|b` is stored (edits_test.go:1561). Say an odd run of backslashes; regenerate claude-envoy dist.

The split flag and the TableCell.Alignment write are dead: pmdoc's parseTableRow takes each cell's alignment from the table's Alignments by index (parse.go:790, 809), and nothing reads TableCell.Alignment. The loop's one job is trimming the row to the table's width, by walking siblings (not ChildCount, given the finding above). Same loop as the fix, so fix it there.

codeSpanText groups a code span by writtenMarks while inlineCodeFence takes every adjacent code node: a drift risk only; both agents' probes of adjacent code under different marks and links read back correctly. Unifying it changes an older path's fences.

Tester observation: a refusal beside adjacent browser-left code quotes the merged span text; conservative and correct.
